basis: The cooperation agreement of May 2025 sets the arrangements for cooperating with the European Labour Authority, which this issue covers.
The government states the draft law harmonises national legislation with Regulation (EU) 2019/1149 for cooperation with the Authority.
The government states the dialogue with the Authority started after signing the agreement, to deepen cooperation.
The government states the capacity building is for the authorities that will cooperate with the Authority.
The government undertakes full transposition of Directive 98/49/EC on supplementary pension rights, the subject of the issue.
The draft amendment to Law No. 198/2020 is listed by the government under supplementary pension rights alignment.
Law No. 109/2025 partially transposes the Open Data Directive, which the Commission found Moldova not aligned with.
The methodological rules apply Law No. 109/2025 on open data.
The government states the open data unit was created under Law No. 109/2025, answering the finding that no authority was responsible for open data.
The draft law on data and data governance transposes the related EU data rules named in the issue.
The government states the extra open data staff are needed to implement the acquis on open data.
The authority plans to strengthen its administrative and human capacities, the shortfall the Commission records.
The authority presents the stronger preliminary complaint assessment as a way to use its limited resources better.
Joining the third-country trusted list answers the 2023 Commission recommendation.
The Commission states the December 2025 amendments align the rules for qualified trust service providers with the European Digital Identity regulation.
The government states Law No. 117/2025 opens the market to EU qualified trust service providers.
The wallet is developed to meet the EU digital identity standards and the Reform Agenda condition.
EVOSign is presented as a free signature service to raise the low use of electronic signatures.
The government presents identity cards carrying a qualified signature as a step to widen adoption of digital identity.
The conformity audit is required before the trust service provider is included in the EU trusted list.
Membership of the EU Digital Identity Cooperation Group is reported by the Commission as part of alignment with eIDAS 2.
Connection to SIENA answers the Commission recommendation to increase data exchange via SIENA.
The biometric database answers the Commission finding that none exists and its call to plan alignment with Eurodac.
The proposed amendments bring the Fingerprint Register in line with Eurodac requirements.
The joint study with eu-LISA assesses interoperability of national systems with SIS, VIS and Eurodac.
The work aims at interoperability of the criminal records register with ECRIS and ECRIS-TCN.
The national visa system is to be interoperable with the EU Visa Information System.
The modernisation of border systems is planned to interconnect them with EU systems, in line with Eurodac.
The Commission states the migration inspectorate systems require upgrades for interoperability with EU systems.
The draft decision connects the vehicle register to EUCARIS for Prüm exchanges.
The draft decision sets up the system for cross-border electronic exchange in judicial cooperation.
The tax service IT programme aims at interconnection and interoperability with EU tax systems, which the Commission found missing.
The roadmap sets the timetable for interoperability with EU information systems.
The planned connections cover VIES and other EU tax information systems.
Connection to the CCN gateway is a prerequisite for EU tax system exchanges.
Connection to TESTA answers the 2023 Commission recommendation linked to CECIS.
The Commission asks Moldova to connect to CECIS.
The Commission requires the Excise Movement and Control System.
The Commission requires the System for the Exchange of Excise Data.
The single liaison point is to cooperate through the Internal Market Information System.
The programmes support SMEs to digitalise their operations, the subject of the issue.
The digital innovation hub is set up to support business digitalisation; the issue covers little use of such hubs.
Association to the Digital Europe Programme opens EU digital programmes to Moldovan applicants.
The national contact point helps applicants use the Digital Europe Programme.
The Reform Agenda reform aims to increase digital government-to-business services, which the Reform Agenda finds sluggish.
The State Register of Legal Units is part of the Reform Agenda step on digital business services.
The life events methodology is part of the Reform Agenda step on digital business services.
Reorganising services around life events is part of the Reform Agenda reform on digital services.
The Commission states the CUPS were set up to respond to persistently low demand for e-services.
The ODA information system answers the Commission key recommendation to digitalise ODA processes.
The employment agency system aims at fully digitalised services by 2027.
The new system answers the Commission recommendations to re-engineer and replace the e-procurement system.
The procurement programme action plan includes re-engineering the e-procurement system.
The concept of the State Register of Public Procurement system frames the new e-procurement system.
Electronic invoicing is one of the modules the Reform Agenda requires of the new system.
The 2026 report states that SIENA was rolled out and that exchanges through it increased.
Promo-LEX states that proactive access was strengthened through the adoption of the open data law.
The ministry report states that the contact point assistance improved applicants capacity to access European digital funding.
The 2025 report states that the launch of Moldova Instant Payments is helping lower transaction costs and support small entrepreneurs.
The government reports that demand for and use of electronic signatures increased substantially when the health information system was implemented.
The 2026 report states that uptake of e-services increased significantly, including in rural areas where 118 CUPS were set up to respond to low demand.
The Court of Accounts follow-up audit states the impact of the permits system as accessibility of permit services through process automation.
The Commission release decision states that the Reform Agenda objective of digitalising 75% of business-related services was achieved.
The strategy implementation report states that 2023 results show significant progress in digitalising public services.
The strategy implementation report states that 41 citizen services and 4 business services were digitalised through the project in 2023.
